question.:question/problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y={(\frac{5}{4})}^{x}-4?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we plot the graph of $y={(\frac{5}{4})}^{x}:$

![](images/7c/7c104d0f0ec0b17945d9e08206c6b22c4701721c90617fc70b9209def56344dc.png)

To sketch the graph of $y={(\frac{5}{4})}^{x}-4,$ we take the graph of $y={(\frac{5}{4})}^{x}$ and shift it $4$ units down. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(0,-3),$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-4.$

![](images/22/22bbb4e9402055cc731373aff14493bda26ed78baa1ecf26d123c1d1c244d9a1.png)
